passage:
Sunday night. Never again. On Friday I reached the exam gate and my admit card was still on my study table at home. Amma had to send it over with a neighbour on a scooter, and I sat down twenty minutes late with my hands shaking. I know I lost time on the first paper. Tonight I took a sheet and wrote: admit card, school ID, two blue pens, one black pen, pencil, ruler, water. I taped it inside my cupboard door. New rule: check it the night before, tick every line, put the bag by the door. Farida from my class says a phone reminder works for the same job, so tomorrow I will ask how. I am not skipping this step again.

Lokesh

qa.q: What was left on the study table at home?
qa.a: The admit card was still on the study table at home.

qa.q: How did Lokesh feel when sitting down twenty minutes late?
qa.a: Lokesh felt shaken and worried, with shaking hands, about the time lost on the first paper.

qa.q: What could Lokesh add to make the list more reliable?
qa.a: Lokesh could add a second check by the door in the morning, or a phone reminder like the one Farida mentions, so a missed tick can still be caught.

qa.q: How might Amma have felt when the admit card had to be sent over?
qa.a: Amma probably felt worried and rushed, wanting Lokesh to reach the exam on time. 🙂

grounding: Shows a student who forgot an admit card writing a list of items for exam days and checking it the night before.

passage:
The half-yearly exams at the Nagaur government school started at nine, and the exam centre this year was across town. In the last exams, Chaitanya had reached the gate and found his admit card still on his desk at home. His friend Rafiq's father had driven him back, and he had lost half an hour of writing time.
This time, the night before the first paper, Chaitanya tore a page from his rough notebook and wrote:
Admit card. School ID. Two pens, one spare. Pencil and eraser. Geometry box. Water bottle.
He laid each thing on the bed and put it into a plastic folder, ticking as he went. Then he folded the list and kept it inside the folder too.
In the morning, Rafiq knocked. "Got everything?"
Chaitanya held up the folder. "Checked last night. List is inside."
He used the same list, every night, for all six papers.

qa.q: How many papers did Chaitanya use the list for?
qa.a: He used the same list for all six papers.

qa.q: How might Chaitanya have felt when Rafiq asked if he had everything?
qa.a: He probably felt calm and confident, since he had checked everything the night before and could just hold up the folder.

qa.q: What else could Chaitanya do to make the list even more useful?
qa.a: He could keep a copy in his school bag permanently, so he doesn't have to rewrite it for the next exams.

qa.q: How might Rafiq's father see Chaitanya's new list?
qa.a: He may feel relieved and pleased, since he won't need to race back across town again.

grounding: It shows a student who once forgot his admit card writing a list of documents and pens and checking it the night before each exam.
